evidence.detail: default order_by is 'active_date DESC, d.finish IS NULL, d.finish' — no unique tiebreaker, so rows with identical finish are ordered arbitrarily by the DB
competition.load_decks calls deck.load_decks(where) without specifying order_by, falling through to the non-stable default
no commit references this issue; the non-stable sort is still present in master

triage.fix_sketch: In decksite/data/deck.py, append ', d.id' to the default order_by string at line 88 (and the identical default at line 159): change 'active_date DESC, d.finish IS NULL, d.finish' to 'active_date DESC, d.finish IS NULL, d.finish, d.id'. The primary key is always unique so the sort becomes fully deterministic. Two one-line changes.
triage.notes: Issue explicitly notes the real answer (swiss tiebreakers) is not scraped; using d.id gives a stable but arbitrary ordering among tied finishers, which is sufficient to stop page flicker.
